source.title: (redacted) Anomalous tokens might disproportionately affect complex language tasks

record.tranche_reason: It examines repeated-token behavior and attention patterns in GPT-2 small as a conceptual test of the induction-head mechanism, but does not use the original training analysis or test induction-head formation.
record.gate_note: The post also cites findings from the SolidGoldMagikarp posts and the induction-head paper; those cited findings are not results of this study. Its task-complexity judgment is subjective. The correction supersedes the rote-repetition comparison in the original text; the post gives no exact corrected accuracy values.
record.test_reason: The post studies glitch-token effects on two repetition tasks in GPT-2 small. The induction-head material reproduces the TransformerLens demo, with a loss drop on repeated random tokens and the attention of L5H5, a head it calls 'known to be an induction head'. It uses this as an illustration and an explanation for the rote-repetition task. It does not test the mechanism (no previous-token composition, no intervention), formation, in-context learning on natural text, or universality.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The original text claimed weak evidence that glitch tokens hurt complex tasks more than simple ones. The correction says a bug in the rote-repetition test invalidated this, and the author now has no strong reason to believe the claim.
record.recipe_differences: It evaluates token repetition and inspects attention patterns in GPT-2 small; it does not reproduce an induction-head training or formation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The corrected rote-repetition comparison differs from the originally reported comparison because of a token-selection mistake; the correction gives no exact rerun accuracies.

fits_no_version.finding: In instructed repetition, accuracy was 34% for normal tokens and 16% for anomalous tokens over 1000 trials.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Glitch tokens reduce GPT-2 small's accuracy on instructed repetition.

fits_no_version.finding: The correction says that after fixing the token-selection bug, the relative performance decrease is similar for anomalous and non-anomalous tokens. The rote-repetition comparison originally reported 91% vs 90% (summary) or 92% vs 91% (body).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Glitch tokens do not disproportionately impair complex tasks relative to rote, induction-driven repetition.

record.problems: The post says it used only two tasks, judged their complexity subjectively, and ran 1000 trials per experiment. The correction identifies a token-selection mistake in the rote-repetition experiment and gives no corrected accuracy figures. Attention-pattern results are qualitative, without a reported intervention.
record.rows_left_out: No applicable results were omitted. The original rote-repetition accuracy statements are excluded because the correction says that experiment tested the wrong token type.

untested.parts: The post does not test composition with a previous-token head, an attention-only model, or causal evidence. It only shows the attention of a head already known to be an induction head.
It does not identify induction heads independently. L5H5 in GPT-2 small is taken from prior work.

record.verdict_notes: The induction-head content is a reproduction of the TransformerLens demo, used to explain why rote repetition is a 'simple' task. The post also reports inconsistent rote-repetition figures (91/90 in the summary vs 92/91 in the body), which the correction supersedes.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test whether induction heads form by composing with a previous-token head, and GPT-2 small is not stated to be attention-only.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured loss by token index for a repeated sequence.
rows.baseline: Loss before the sequence starts repeating
rows.value: Loss drops steeply at index 10, where the first repetition occurs
rows.note: The post reports a qualitative loss drop at the repetition point; it does not give numeric loss values.
rows.check: This is a demo of the loss drop on repeated random tokens, reproduced from the TransformerLens demo. It is not a test of V1, which concerns attention-only models and composition, and it is not natural-text in-context learning (V3). No numbers are given.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected the attention pattern of the identified induction head on a repeated sequence.
rows.baseline: Before repetition, tokens attend to the first token
rows.value: After repetition begins, attention follows the repeating tokens diagonally
rows.note: The post identifies this as a known induction head in GPT-2 small. It does not report a causal intervention.
rows.check: The head is pre-identified from prior work as a known induction head, and the result is a qualitative attention plot only. It is an illustration of a cited finding rather than a new test. At most it would bear weakly on V4, but it adds nothing beyond the cited demo.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Inspected a non-induction head's attention pattern on a repeated sequence.
rows.measure: Attention pattern and usefulness for predicting the next token
rows.value: The head attends to tokens described as irrelevant to predicting the next token
rows.note: The post calls this a random, non-induction head and contrasts its pattern with head 5.
rows.check: This is a comparator head shown for illustration. The 'absent' state has no meaning against any version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured exact-match accuracy on instructed repetition of sampled normal tokens.
rows.note: This result concerns anomalous-token effects on instructed repetition, which none of the listed claim versions specifies.
rows.check: This is a glitch-token result and bears on no induction-head version.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measured exact-match accuracy on instructed repetition of sampled anomalous tokens.
rows.note: The post reports lower accuracy for anomalous tokens. The correction does not revise this result.
rows.check: This is a glitch-token result. The 'partial' state is meaningless here. The correction's statement that the relative decrease is similar across token types bears on how this comparison should be read.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Reran rote-repetition experiments after correcting a token-selection mistake.
rows.value: The relative performance decrease is similar across anomalous and non-anomalous tokens
rows.locator: Correction at the start of the post
rows.note: The correction says the earlier rote-repetition task tested non-glitch tokens by mistake. It gives no exact corrected accuracies; the original rote-repetition values are therefore not recorded as corrected results.
rows.check: This is a corrected glitch-token result with no numbers given. It bears on no induction-head version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported loss drop at the first repetition and the layer 5 head 5 attention pattern match repeated-token completion behavior (r1, r2).
